system:
You are an interpretability researcher. You are given a trained neural network: its weights, its architecture and the set of inputs it is used on. Your job is to work out HOW it computes its outputs and to write that down as a CONSTRUCTION that an automatic judge will test.

WHAT A CONSTRUCTION IS
A short, standalone Python file that defines:

  DESCRIPTION = "plain-language account of the mechanism"

  def model(x, iv):
      # x: the inputs, a numpy array [B, n_in]. Must return the network's predicted output, an array [B, n_out].
      # Every named intermediate variable is registered with iv:
      #     v = iv("name", value)        value is an array [B] or [B, k]; iv returns it in the same shape.
      # ALWAYS compute later steps from what iv returned, never from a copy made before the iv call:
      # during intervention tests iv returns a replaced value, and your model must respond to it.
      ...

  ALIGN = {"name": ["site", ...], ...}     # for each variable, the activation site(s) of the network where it lives

The file can use numpy (as np) and math only. It CANNOT see the weights W or run the network: every constant it needs (frequencies, thresholds, coefficients, small tables) must be written into the file as literals, after you have measured them. Limit: 16,000 characters. It is meant to be a compact program that a person can read, not a copy of the network.

A small example of the format, for an unrelated toy network (2 inputs, one hidden layer "h1", 1 output) that outputs max(x1, x2):

  DESCRIPTION = "Outputs max(x1, x2). The hidden layer holds relu(x1 - x2) and x2; the output adds them."
  def model(x, iv):
      gap = iv("gap", np.maximum(x[:, 0] - x[:, 1], 0))
      base = iv("base", x[:, 1])
      return (gap + base)[:, None]
  ALIGN = {"gap": ["h1"], "base": ["h1"]}

HOW THE JUDGE TESTS IT (on inputs held out from fitting)
1. Behaviour: does model(x) make the same decision as the network (largest output; sign if there is one output; if the network makes one decision per position, all of them)?
2. Alignment: at each site in ALIGN the judge fits ONE affine map from the variables you placed there to the real activations (activation = c + variables @ M). So a variable must be related to the activations linearly. If the network encodes a quantity through several nonlinear functions of it (for example a one-hot code, or a few smooth functions of it), the variable should be those functions' values, a few coordinates, not the raw quantity.
3. Substitution: the site's activation is replaced by the construction's prediction (c + variables @ M) and the rest of the network runs. The decisions must survive. Removing the named subspace from the real activation must destroy them. And the variables must be compact: the judge reports how many principal components of the site suffice to keep the decisions, and you may name at most about twice that many dimensions. Huge variables (a lookup table of the inputs) fail this.
4. Interchange, at each site s you align to: the network is run on an input B, but at site s the part of the activation that encodes your variables is replaced by what it is on another input A (the variables are read from the two real activations with a linear probe, and the change (v(A) - v(B)) @ M is added at site s); everything after site s is recomputed. The network's new decision must equal what model(B) returns when iv gives those variables their values from A (need 90%). So the causal wiring of model() must mirror the network: a variable must feed the later variables the way the activation at its site feeds the later sites. A variable placed at several sites is tested at each site separately.
5. Off-manifold tests, which make states that no input produces (need 50% of the cases where the network's decision changes). Two are run at each site, and passing EITHER is enough: partial (each variable at the site is copied from A while the site's other variables keep their values from B; needs several variables at the site) and edit (a random half of the coordinates of everything you named at the site are copied). Both need realistic coefficients in model(), not just the right decision on ordinary inputs. Where the network keeps parts separate (one per position, per input, per feature group), give each part its own variable, with the coordinates that belong together kept together: copying whole parts keeps every part at a value it really takes.
A site is verified when it passes 3-5. The network's sites are grouped into STAGES (the successive steps of its computation); a stage is explained when one of its sites is verified. The construction is COMPLETE when it behaves like the network and every stage is explained. That is the goal, reached one stage at a time, with variables that are as low-dimensional as you can make them.

YOUR TOOLS
- python(code): runs in a persistent session (variables stay between calls). Available: W (dict of weight arrays), X (all inputs the network is used on, [N, n_in]), run(x) -> outputs, acts(x) -> {site: activations [B, width]} (every site, exact: you never need to re-implement the forward pass), SITES, np, scipy, sklearn. Print what you want to see; output is cut at about 8,000 characters, so print summaries, not raw arrays.
- submit(code): sends a construction file to the judge and returns its report. The report is the fastest way to learn what is right: it tells you, site by site and variable by variable, what passes and what fails.

SUBMIT EARLY, THEN IMPROVE STAGE BY STAGE
Do not try to understand everything before you submit. A construction that explains only one stage is a valid submission, and partial constructions are expected along the way: stages are added one at a time. Make your first submission within your first 6 steps, as soon as you know what the network does and have one candidate variable at one site. After that, submit whenever you have changed something. If you go 6 steps without submitting, you will be required to submit what you have. Explain the easy stages first and leave the hardest stage for last.

HOW TO WORK
1. Find out WHAT the network does: run it on its inputs and find the rule relating inputs to outputs.
2. Find out HOW, stage by stage. Look at the weights themselves for structure (which rows or columns matter, low rank, sparsity, repeated or regular patterns along an index, groups of similar units), and at the activations at each site as functions of the input. Look for a small set of quantities that each site's activations are simple (linear) functions of, and check candidates by regression before you rely on them. Let the numbers decide; do not assume a mechanism because it is familiar.
3. Write the construction with one or more variables for each stage, computed from the previous stage's variables. Measure the constants with python, write them into the file, submit, read the report, and fix what fails.
4. If a site fails, investigate why with python (what does the activation depend on that your variables miss? is the variable used by the network at that site at all?) before resubmitting. You can reproduce any of the judge's tests yourself with run and acts. A variable that is present at a site but not used by what comes after should be given its own name and not fed forward in model().
Keep each message short. Do the thinking with code. When the judge reports VERIFIED AND COMPLETE, or you are certain you cannot improve further, reply with a short final summary and no tool call.
task:
THE NETWORK
A one-layer transformer with no LayerNorm and no biases. Vocabulary of 114 tokens; the input is a sequence of 3 tokens; the output is 113 logits read at the last position.
  x = W_E[tokens] + W_pos                     W_E: 114 x 128, W_pos: 3 x 128
  attention: 4 heads of size 32, causal       W_Q, W_K, W_V: 4 x 128 x 32 (per head: d_model x d_head), W_O: 4 x 32 x 128
  x = x + sum_h softmax(q k^T / sqrt(32)) v W_O[h]
  x = x + relu(x @ W_in) @ W_out              W_in: 128 x 512, W_out: 512 x 128
  logits = x[last] @ W_U                      W_U: 128 x 113

Weight tensors in W: W_E (114, 128) = token embedding (row = token); W_pos (3, 128) = position embedding; W_Q (4, 128, 32) = queries [head, d_model, d_head]; W_K (4, 128, 32) = keys [head, d_model, d_head]; W_V (4, 128, 32) = values [head, d_model, d_head]; W_O (4, 32, 128) = head outputs [head, d_head, d_model]; W_in (128, 512) = MLP input (column = neuron); W_out (512, 128) = MLP output (row = neuron); W_U (128, 113) = unembedding (column = output class)
(226,048 parameters.)

ACTIVATION SITES (name, width, what it is) by stage:
  stage: embedding
    embed.0  [128]  token + position embedding at position 0
    embed.1  [128]  token + position embedding at position 1
    embed.2  [128]  token + position embedding at position 2
  stage: attention
    attn_pattern  [12]  attention weights of the last position: for each head, its weight on each of the 3 positions, flattened as head * 3 + position
    attn_out  [128]  what the attention layer adds at the last position
    resid_mid  [128]  residual stream at the last position after attention
  stage: mlp neurons
    mlp_pre  [512]  MLP neurons before ReLU (last position)
    mlp_post  [512]  MLP neurons after ReLU (last position)
  stage: readout
    mlp_out  [128]  what the MLP adds to the residual stream
    resid_post  [128]  residual stream at the last position after the MLP
  stage: output  (not a site you can align to; model() returns it)
    out  [113]  the network's output

THE INPUTS
The network is used on every input [i, j, 113] with i and j each ranging over 0..112 (12,769 inputs).

You are not told what the network does or what its inputs and outputs mean. Find out.

Begin.

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Task: input [i, j, 113]; the network outputs logits over c in 0..112 with the argmax "
               "at c = (i+j) mod 113. First stage: token embeddings are Fourier features of the token "
               "index at frequencies 8, 11, 23, 25 out of 113 (8 real dimensions); position embeddings are "
               "constants. So embed.0 is a fixed affine function of [cos/sin at 4 freqs of i], embed.1 the "
               "same for j, embed.2 is constant.")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    e2 = iv("e2", np.ones((x.shape[0], 1)))
    c = (x[:, 0] + x[:, 1]) % N
    out = np.full((x.shape[0], N), -10.0)
    out[np.arange(x.shape[0]), c] = 10.0
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "e2": ["embed.2"]}

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]. The network's argmax is c = (i+j) mod 113. Embeddings: token t<113 is "
               "a Fourier code at 4 frequencies (8, 11, 23, 25) out of 113; position embeddings are constants. "
               "The last position's query is fixed, so attention mixes the two Fourier codes; the MLP then "
               "forms products (angle addition) and the unembedding reads cos(2*pi*f*(c - (i+j))/113) for "
               "f in {8,11,23,25}. This file names the two embedding Fourier codes and computes the output "
               "from them by the product (angle-addition) identity.")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR):
        ci, si = e0[:, 2*k], e0[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = e1[:, 2*k], e1[:, 2*k+1]
        cs = ci*cj - si*sj
        ss = si*cj + ci*sj
        out += cs[:, None]*C[f][None, :] + ss[:, None]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"]}

import numpy as np
np.set_printoptions(precision=3, suppress=True)
N=113; FR=[8,11,23,25]
Xs = X[::13]
A = acts(Xs)
ao = A['attn_out']; ii=Xs[:,0].astype(float); jj=Xs[:,1].astype(float)
def feats(v):
    cols=[np.ones_like(v)]
    for f in FR:
        a=2*np.pi*f*v/N; cols += [np.cos(a), np.sin(a)]
    return np.stack(cols,axis=1)
Fi, Fj = feats(ii), feats(jj)
def r2(y, Xd):
    coef,_,_,_ = np.linalg.lstsq(Xd, y, rcond=None)
    pred = Xd@coef
    return 1-((y-pred)**2).sum()/((y-y.mean(0))**2).sum()
print("attn_out ~ [1,Fi,Fj]:", r2(ao, np.hstack([Fi,Fj])).round(4))
# products of Fi x Fj
outer = np.einsum('bi,bj->bij', Fi, Fj).reshape(len(ii),-1)
print("attn_out ~ Fi x Fj (bilinear):", r2(ao, outer).round(4))
print("attn_out ~ Fi,Fj,Fi x Fj:", r2(ao, np.hstack([Fi,Fj,outer])).round(4))

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; the network's argmax is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is encoded as a "
               "Fourier code at 4 frequencies (8, 11, 23, 25) of 113 (cos and sin); position embeddings are "
               "constants. The last position's query is fixed, so attention at the last position produces "
               "attn_out ~= g(i) + g(j) + const, i.e. it just carries the two tokens' Fourier codes into the "
               "residual stream (a linear function of [cos/sin of i, cos/sin of j], 91% of its variance). "
               "The MLP multiplies them (angle addition), the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113). "
               "This file names the two embedding codes and the attention stage's carried codes; the output "
               "is computed from the attention variable by the product (angle-addition) identity.")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR):
        ci, si = att[:, 2*k], att[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = att[:, 8+2*k], att[:, 8+2*k+1]
        cs = ci*cj - si*sj
        ss = si*cj + ci*sj
        out += cs[:, None]*C[f][None, :] + ss[:, None]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "att": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"]}

2-3. SITES   explained = share of the activation's variance the variables explain;  substitute = network decision kept when the activation is replaced by the construction's prediction;  keep = when only the named subspace of the real activation is kept;  remove = when the named subspace is removed (should be LOW) vs a random subspace of equal size;  mean-ablate = when the whole site is replaced by its mean
  embed.0     (8 dims named of 128; 7 principal components suffice; e0): explained 0.874 | substitute 100.0% | keep 100.0% | remove 0.6% (random 100.0%) | mean-ablate 0.9%

4. INTERVENTIONS   interchange = everything named at the site is copied from another input's run (need 90%). Then tests that make states no input produces (need 50% of the cases where the decision changed): partial = one variable is copied while the site's other variables stay; edit = a random half of the coordinates of everything named at the site are copied. import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; the network's argmax is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is encoded as a "
               "Fourier code at 4 frequencies (8, 11, 23, 25) of 113 (cos and sin); position embeddings are "
               "constants and the last position's query is fixed. Attention at the last position carries the "
               "two tokens' codes into the residual stream: attn_out ~= g(i) + g(j) + const, a linear function "
               "of [cos/sin of i, cos/sin of j]. The MLP multiplies the two codes (angle addition), so mlp_pre / "
               "mlp_post / mlp_out hold the 'sum code' cos/sin of (i+j) at the same 4 frequencies; the readout "
               "is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113). This file names the embedding codes, the attention-carried codes, "
               "and the sum code at the MLP and readout stages.")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(a):
    out = np.zeros((a.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = a[:, 2*k], a[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = a[:, 8+2*k], a[:, 8+2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    code = iv("code", sumcode(att))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "att": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "code": ["mlp_pre", "mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

FRQ=[8,11,23,25]
def basis(t):
    t=np.asarray(t,dtype=float); cols=[np.ones_like(t)]
    for f in FRQ: cols += [np.cos(2*np.pi*f*t/N), np.sin(2*np.pi*f*t/N)]

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; the network's argmax is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is encoded as a "
               "Fourier code at 4 frequencies (8, 11, 23, 25) of 113 (cos and sin); position embeddings are "
               "constants and the last position's query is fixed. Attention at the last position carries each "
               "token's code into the residual stream: attn_out ~= g(i) + g(j) + const, where the position-0 "
               "part depends on token i and the position-1 part on token j. The MLP multiplies the two carried "
               "codes (angle addition), so the sum code cos/sin of (i+j) appears at the MLP and readout stages; "
               "the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113). This file names the embedding codes, the two carried "
               "codes (kept separate: one per token/position), and the sum code.")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    ai = iv("atti", e0)
    aj = iv("attj", e1)
    code = np.zeros((x.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = ai[:, 2*k], ai[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = aj[:, 2*k], aj[:, 2*k+1]
        code[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        code[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    code = iv("code", code)
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "atti": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "attj": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"], "code": ["mlp_pre", "mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

import numpy as np
np.set_printoptions(precision=3, suppress=True)
N=113
WE,WP,WQ,WK,WV,WO = W['W_E'],W['W_pos'],W['W_Q'],W['W_K'],W['W_V'],W['W_O']
Mh={h: WV[h]@WO[h] for h in range(4)}
sq=np.sqrt(32)
qq={h:(WE[113]+WP[2])@WQ[h] for h in range(4)}
# exact w using full 113-feature interpolation
t=np.arange(N)
Fd=np.exp(-2j*np.pi*np.outer(t,t)/N)/np.sqrt(N)
ah={h:(WE[:114]@WK[h]@qq[h])/sq for h in range(4)}
coE={h: Fd@(Fd.conj().T@ah[h][:N]) for h in range(4)}  # exact reconstruction via full basis

    true=run(X).argmax(1); mean=act.mean(0); M=co[1:]

    rem=(fwd(X,{sited:lambda a: mean+dev-proj}).argmax(1)==true).mean()
    sub=(fwd(X,{sited:lambda a: recon}).argmax(1)==true).mean()

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; the network's argmax is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is encoded as a "
               "Fourier code at 4 frequencies (8, 11, 23, 25) of 113 (cos and sin); position embeddings are "
               "constants and the last position's query is fixed. Attention at the last position carries the "
               "two tokens' codes into the residual stream; the MLP multiplies the two codes (angle addition), "
               "so mlp_post / mlp_out / resid_post hold the 'sum code' cos/sin of (i+j) at the same 4 "
               "frequencies; the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113).")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(a):
    out = np.zeros((a.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = a[:, 2*k], a[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = a[:, 8+2*k], a[:, 8+2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    code = iv("code", sumcode(att))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "att": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "code": ["mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

def myfwd(tok, patch=None):
    # tok: [B,3] ints; patch: dict site-> (array[B, width] to REPLACE the activation at that site used downstream)
    B = tok.shape[0]
    x = W_E[tok] + W_pos[None,:,:]           # [B,3,128]
    sites = {}
    sites['embed.0'] = x[:,0]; sites['embed.1'] = x[:,1]; sites['embed.2'] = x[:,2]
    if patch and 'embed.0' in patch: x = x.copy(); x[:,0] = patch['embed.0']
    if patch and 'embed.1' in patch: x = x.copy(); x[:,1] = patch['embed.1']
    q = x[:,2] @ W_Q                              # [B,4,32]
    k = np.einsum('bpd,hde->bhpe', x, W_K)        # [B,4,3,32]
    v = np.einsum('bpd,hde->bhpe', x, W_V)
    lo = np.einsum('bhe,bhpe->bhp', q, k)/np.sqrt(32)
    lo = lo - 1e9*np.array([0.,0.,0.])[None,None,:]  # causal: all positions <=2 visible
    w = np.exp(lo - lo.max(-1, keepdims=True)); w = w/w.sum(-1, keepdims=True)
    sites['attn_pattern'] = w.reshape(B,12)
    ao = np.einsum('bhp,bhpe,hed->bd', w, v, W_O)
    sites['attn_out'] = ao
    rmid = x[:,2] + ao
    sites['resid_mid'] = rmid
    if patch and 'attn_out' in patch: rmid = x[:,2] + patch['attn_out']
    if patch and 'resid_mid' in patch: rmid = patch['resid_mid']
    if patch and 'attn_pattern' in patch:
        w2 = patch['attn_pattern'].reshape(B,4,3)
        rmid = x[:,2] + np.einsum('bhp,bhpe,hed->bd', w2, v, W_O)
    pre = rmid @ W_in
    sites['mlp_pre'] = pre
    post = np.maximum(pre,0)
    sites['mlp_post'] = post
    mo = post @ W_out
    sites['mlp_out'] = mo
    rp = rmid + mo
    sites['resid_post'] = rp
    return rp @ W_U, sites

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; argmax output is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is a Fourier code at "
               "frequencies 8, 11, 23, 25 of 113 (cos and sin); positions/last-position query are constants. "
               "Attention at the last position mixes the two tokens' codes into the residual stream (a "
               "nonlinear, softmax-weighted mixture, well described by a linear function of [code(i), code(j)]). "
               "The MLP multiplies the two codes (angle addition) so mlp_post/mlp_out/resid_post carry the sum "
               "code cos/sin of (i+j); the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113).")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25, 5]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(a):
    D = 2*len(FR)
    out = np.zeros((a.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = a[:, 2*k], a[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = a[:, D+2*k], a[:, D+2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    code = iv("code", sumcode(att))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR[:4]):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "att": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "code": ["mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

def knn_dec(Z, dec, k=1):
    out = np.zeros(len(Z), int); dd=np.zeros(len(Z))
    for st in range(0, len(Z), 400):

        D = ((blk[:,None,:]-Z[None,:,:])**2).sum(-1)

        j = D.argmin(1); out[st:st+400] = dec[j]; dd[st:st+400]=np.sqrt(D[np.arange(len(blk)), j])
    return out, dd

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; argmax output is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is a Fourier code at "
               "frequencies 8, 11, 23, 25 of 113 (cos and sin); positions/last-position query are constants. "
               "Attention at the last position mixes the two tokens' codes into the residual stream (a "
               "softmax-weighted mixture, well described by a linear function of [code(i), code(j)]). The MLP "
               "multiplies the two codes (angle addition) so mlp_post/mlp_out/resid_post carry the sum code "
               "cos/sin of (i+j); the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113).")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25, 5]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(a):
    D = 2*len(FR)
    out = np.zeros((a.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = a[:, 2*k], a[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = a[:, D+2*k], a[:, D+2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    code = iv("code", sumcode(att))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR[:4]):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "att": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "code": ["mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; argmax output is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is a Fourier code at "
               "frequencies 8, 11, 23, 25 of 113 (cos and sin); positions/last-position query are constants. "
               "Attention at the last position mixes the two tokens' codes into the residual stream (a "
               "softmax-weighted mixture, well described by a linear function of [code(i), code(j)]). The MLP "
               "multiplies the two codes (angle addition) so mlp_post/mlp_out/resid_post carry the sum code "
               "cos/sin of (i+j); the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113).")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25, 5]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(a):
    D = 2*len(FR)
    out = np.zeros((a.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = a[:, 2*k], a[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = a[:, D+2*k], a[:, D+2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    att = iv("att", np.hstack([e0, e1]))
    code = iv("code", sumcode(att))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR[:4]):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

import numpy as np

DESCRIPTION = ("Input [i, j, 113]; argmax output is c = (i+j) mod 113. Token t<113 is a Fourier code at "
               "frequencies 8, 11, 23, 25 of 113 (cos and sin); positions/last-position query are constants. "
               "Attention at the last position passes the two tokens' codes into the residual stream (one part "
               "per token, a softmax-weighted mixture, well described by a linear function of [code(i), code(j)]). "
               "The MLP multiplies the two codes (angle addition) so mlp_post/mlp_out/resid_post carry the sum "
               "code cos/sin of (i+j); the readout is cos(2*pi*f*(c-(i+j))/113).")

N = 113
FR = [8, 11, 23, 25, 5]
C = {f: np.cos(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
S = {f: np.sin(2*np.pi*f*np.arange(N)/N) for f in FR}
D = 2*len(FR)

def feats(v):
    cols = []
    for f in FR:
        a = 2.0*np.pi*f*v/N
        cols.append(np.cos(a)); cols.append(np.sin(a))
    return np.stack(cols, axis=1)

def sumcode(ai, aj):
    out = np.zeros((ai.shape[0], 8))
    for k in range(4):
        ci, si = ai[:, 2*k], ai[:, 2*k+1]
        cj, sj = aj[:, 2*k], aj[:, 2*k+1]
        out[:, 2*k] = ci*cj - si*sj
        out[:, 2*k+1] = si*cj + ci*sj
    return out

def model(x, iv):
    i = x[:, 0].astype(float); j = x[:, 1].astype(float)
    e0 = iv("e0", feats(i))
    e1 = iv("e1", feats(j))
    ai = iv("ai", e0)
    aj = iv("aj", e1)
    code = iv("code", sumcode(ai, aj))
    out = np.zeros((x.shape[0], N))
    for k, f in enumerate(FR[:4]):
        out += code[:, [2*k]]*C[f][None, :] + code[:, [2*k+1]]*S[f][None, :]
    return out

ALIGN = {"e0": ["embed.0"], "e1": ["embed.1"], "ai": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"],
         "aj": ["attn_out", "resid_mid"], "code": ["mlp_post", "mlp_out", "resid_post"]}

# LAB NOTES

## 1. What the network does
Input `[i, j, 113]` for all i,j ∈ 0..112. Groups (token 0..112 = digit/Fourier symbols, token 113 = pad). Argmax of the 113 logits = `c = (i+j) mod 113` (100% match). Out is a readout `cos(2π f (c - s)/113)` at frequencies f ∈ {8, 11, 23, 25} (Fourier analysis of logits for fixed s = i+j showed exactly these 4 freqs); residual explains only ~10% of logit variance, i.e. decision is fully determined by s = i+j mod 113.

## 2. Established facts (numbers)

### Embeddings (stage 1, VERIFIED at embed.0, embed.1)
- `W_E[t]` for t<113 has energy almost entirely at 4 frequencies: 8, 11, 23, 25 (out of N=113) — DFT energy per freq: 32.6, 23.4, 26.9, 32.6; all other freqs ≤0.7. So each token is a cosine/sine code: 8 real dims, and `embed.p` is an affine function of `[cos,sin](2π f t/113)` for f in {8,11,23,25}. 7 PCs suffice (freq 8 and multiples are real/imag pairs).
- `embed.2` is identical for every input (only pad token 113 + fixed W_pos), so it holds no variable (judge ignores it).
- `W_pos` is a constant per position; last position's query is fixed (only token 113 at position 2).
- Var names used: `e0` (8 dims, feats of i) at embed.0, `e1` at embed.1. These pass everything (explained 0.874; substitute 100%; remove 0.6%; interchange 99.9%).

### Attention (stage 2 — NOT YET VERIFIED, this is the current blocker)
- Exact mechanism: `a_h(t) = (W_E[t] @ W_K[h] @ q_h)/sqrt(32)`, with fixed `q_h = (W_E[113]+W_pos[2]) @ W_Q[h]`; position offsets `offs_h[p] = (W_pos[p] @ W_K[h] @ q_h)/sqrt(32)`. Logits at last position: `lo_h = [a_h(i)+offs_h[0], a_h(j)+offs_h[1], a_h(113)+offs_h[2]]`, `w = softmax(lo_h)`. This reproduces `attn_pattern` EXACTLY (error 4e-16) when a_h is exact. `attn_out` = `einsum('hq,hqe,hed->bd', w, v, W_O)` with `v = (W_E[tok]+W_pos[p]) @ W_V[h]`. I have a working full re-implementation `fwd(x, mod)` in python matching `run` to 1e-14 (see below).
- Important: `a_h(t)` is NOT a low-order Fourier function of t — its DFT energy is spread over ALL frequencies (h0 top freqs only ~1.4% each), because the embedding's 4-freq code and the key's random 128-dim structure make `a_h` effectively a random function of t. Hence one cannot compute softmax weights from a few Fourier features; the weights must be computed from the *variables*.
- Key observed structure: `V^T T_h(t)` (token part of head h's output projected on the top 10 PCs of attn_out) is also NOT low-frequency (energy flat across freqs) → the →128 output directions are effectively random functions of t too.
- Because a_h(t) is a semicircle-ish/random function of t, attention weights saturate (near one-hot in places) and `attn_out` contains only ~94% of its variance in an additive `A(i)+A(j)+const` model with FULL per-token functions; 10 PCs explain 95.5% of variance but keeping only those 10 explains decisions only 91.4%.
- `attn_out` / `resid_mid` (identical since resid_mid = embed.2 + attn_out): SVD spectrum flat — PC var fractions: 10 PCs = 95.5%, 16 PCs = 99.94%. **16 dims are needed for substitute/keep to reach 100%** (V10: keep/dev 91.4%, sub 91.4%; V16: keep 100%, rem 0.8%, sub 100%). Judge says "10 principal components suffice" (its own PCA rule), so at most ~20 dims may be named — 16 is OK but that's 2×16 = 32 > 20 limit? (judge complained only when >2×). Best plan: name 16 dims = 8 for the i-part and 8 for the j-part, or 16 total split 8/8.
- Best linear description found: `attn_out ≈ const + u_i(out of i's code, 8 dims) + v_j(8 dims)`, where u = Σ_h w_h0·(token part of h's output for token i + pos-0 offset) and similarly for v; reconstructing z = (attn_out−mean)@V16 from (u,v) gave explained 0.9915 (with fitted w) and 0.9939 (with exact w). The remaining error comes from softmax-weight inaccuracy (needs exact a_h).

### MLP (stage 3, VERIFIED at mlp_post)
- MLP multiplies the two carried codes: `mlp_out ≈ f(s)` where s=(i+j) mod 113: `mlp_out ~ [1, cos/sin of s at 8,11,23,25]` gives R²=0.899; `mlp_post` with the "code" (8 dims: cos/sin of s at 8,11,23,25) explains 0.155 but keep=99.5%, substitute 100% — VERIFIED. `mlp_out` (8-d code): explained 0.899, keep 100%, sub 100% VERIFIED. `resid_post`: explained 0.863, keep 100%, sub 100% VERIFIED.
- mlp_out mean part is huge (norm 136) — a constant offset; the s-dependence is the 8-d code with amplitudes ~34,49,23,21 (cos/sin pairs) on top.
- `mlp_pre` FAILS: code explains only 2.1%, keep 15.8%, substitute 87.6%, and interchange of code changes the network's decision only 5.3% of the time — **mlp_pre is not a site worth explaining** (the judge's mlp-stage verification already comes from mlp_post). Do NOT name `code` at mlp_pre (it fails and the network is insensitive there). Actually careful: judge needs one site per stage; mlp_post works.
- Angle-addition identity used in model: given per-frequency (c_i,s_i) and (c_j,s_j), code = (c_i c_j − s_i s_j, s_i c_j + c_i s_j).

### Readout (stage 4, VERIFIED at mlp_out, resid_post)
- logits = resid_post @ W_U with resid_post ≈ const + Σ_{k} [code_cos_k · C_f + code_sin_k · S_f] where C_f[c]=cos(2π f (c)/113), S_f[c]=sin(...). (Sign convention: the argmax is at c = c_i c_j ... i.e. cos of (c−(i+j)); my construction with cos/sin of s times cos/sin of c peaks at c = s if signs are (cos,(−sin)) or similar — in my submitted file I used `out += code_cos*C + code_sin*S` and got 100% same decision, so that form works.)

## 3. What failed and why
- First submission: fake logit one-hot → decisions fine but embeddings' interchange 0% (model must respond to the variables). Fixed by computing output as a function of the variables via the product identity → 99.9%.
- Adding `att` = hstack([e0,e1]) at attn_out: substitute 80.8% (<90), interchange 44%. Reason: attn_out is not a linear function of the Fourier codes of i and j (attention weights are a strongly nonlinear function of the tokens) — the Fourier-code variables can only explain 91% of attn_out, and residual errors matter because attn_out is not what carries the decision (it goes through the MLP which multiplies). Resid_mid is just a constant offset from attn_out → same numbers.
- Splitting into `atti`/`attj` (each a copy of e0/e1): same failures; partial tests 4% because the copies don't reflect the actual weight nonlinearity.
- `code` at mlp_pre: fails (see above).
- Mixing pre/post iv copies in model (e.g., compute code from a copy of att rather than the iv-returned value) — must always compute from the iv-returned value; but NOTE the real problem at attn_out is fidelity, not wiring.

## 4. Latest judge report (submission #4, 3 of 4 stages verified)
PASS: embed.0/embed.1 (all tests); code at mlp_post (sub 100%, interchange 100%/100%, edit 74%/71%), mlp_out (100%,100%,73%), resid_post (100%,100%,73%).
FAIL: attn_out & resid_mid — substitute 80.8% (need 90%), interchange 42–44% (need 90%), partial 4% (need 50%), edit 24.6% (need 50%, either one suffices); mlp_pre (ignore).
STAGES: embedding VERIFIED; mlp neurons VERIFIED (mlp_post); readout VERIFIED (mlp_out, resid_post); attention NOT.

## 5. What to try next
Make the attn_out variable a faithful 16-dim description of `attn_out`:
- Plan A (best): compute exact attention weights inside the model from the variables. Need `a_h(tok)`, `offs_h[p]`, and the two output maps. To keep the variable *linear* in the site, name 16 variables = [8 dims for i-part, 8 dims for j-part] defined as `u = Σ_h w_h0 · T_h(i)` and `v = Σ_h w_h1 · T_h(j)` projected on V16 basis. Since w depends on a_h(i), a_h(j), which must be computed from the *inputs* (i,j) — but i,j are only available through e0/e1 (8 dims), which do NOT determine a_h(t) (a_h is a random function of t). So w cannot be computed from the variables. => Plan A impossible unless we allow the model to read integer tokens from x directly (which IS allowed: model(x) gets x!). YES — model(x, iv) has access to x, so it can compute exact a_h(t) via an in-file lookup approximation. But constants can't be 113×4 floats? That's fine size-wise (113*4 numbers ≈ small if rounded to 2 decimals: but a_h must be accurate to ~1e-3 for correct softmax; and, crucially, the model's *variable* is what feeds later stages, so the 16-dim u/v must be a linear function at the site: it is, if u/v are defined via the same V16 basis).
  Concretely: with 16 exact dims computed as z = (attn_out_exact(x) − mean)@V16 — that is a lookup table of the inputs (2×113 tables per dim = too big/huge variable) BUT it can be computed from x arithmetically if I hardcode a_h tables (113 values × 4 heads, rounded). Simplest workable variant: hardcode the 8-dim "token code" per head? No.
  Practical approach: hardcode per-head arrays `A_h[114]` (a_h at each token, rounded to 4 decimals), `OFF[p]`, and the maps: u/v 16-dim via a fixed 128→16 basis. Then z computed from x, and ALIGN with `z` (16 dims) at attn_out/resid_mid. Var is 16 dims = at the "twice 10" limit (judge reported 10 PCs suffice → up to 20 dims allowed). This should give substitute/keep 100%, interchange ~100% (if the 16-dim z determines the rest — it doesn't: MLP reads the full attn_out; but keep=100% and decisions depend only on s so probably fine), edit might still be <50% but partial (2 vars: u and v, each 8 dims) should pass if swapping u alone is realistic (it is: u really ranges over its real values, so swapping the i-part while keeping the j-part is a real state → network gives s' = i_A + j_B, and model predicts the same).
  So aim: `u` = 8 dims from i only, `v` = 8 dims from j only, each within attn_out's span. Implement u = Σ_h w_h0(i,j?) — w depends on both, so u is not a pure function of i. But swap semantics: judge swaps u from A into B's state; network result = attention with i from A, j from B → s' = i_A + j_B.
